subject.title: [Feature]: Add gateway-side circuit breaker for unhealthy sessions after consecutive failures

question: Should OpenClaw core own a unified session-health circuit-breaker receipt for consecutive no-progress attempts, and what default, persistence, recovery, and UI/operator contract should it expose?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the remaining choice crosses failure taxonomy, config defaults, persisted session state, recovery actions, and UI/operator surfacing, which automation cannot safely choose as a product contract.

options.title: Define unified session-health receipts
options.body: Specify failure_signature, consecutive_failures, last_success_at, retry_admitted, suggested_recovery, persistence, and recovery semantics before implementation.

options.title: Land a narrow no-progress breaker
options.body: Add only a bounded consecutive no-progress counter in the embedded run loop and leave receipts, UI, cooldowns, and auto-rotation as follow-up work.

options.title: Defer to narrower guards
options.body: Keep idle-timeout, tool-loop, compaction, provider, cron, and subagent guard tracks separate and narrow or close this umbrella later.

recommendation.title: Define unified session-health receipts
recommendation.body: Specify failure_signature, consecutive_failures, last_success_at, retry_admitted, suggested_recovery, persistence, and recovery semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current adjacent retry and breaker code in this checkout is tied most directly to Vincent Koc's recent source history.
